statement.excerpt: The $122 billion funding round from March will be insufficient to cover these costs, and it will require, at the very least, another $250 billion in funding by the end of the year.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns financing required, not merely financing raised. A voluntary capital raise does not establish that the entire amount was necessary.
Additional funding excludes the March round and secondary share sales whose proceeds do not go to OpenAI.
I treat the financing requirement as an estimate derived from the author's discussion of projected costs and commitments, rather than an accounting result reported by OpenAI.
The ordinary reading requires a cash-flow and payment schedule. Multiyear commitments are not assumed payable entirely in 2026.
criteria.support_condition: Financial records establish that the March round cannot cover the referenced costs and that OpenAI requires at least USD 250 billion of additional external financing by December 31, 2026, after accounting for existing liquidity, operating cash receipts, and payment timing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Complete records establish that OpenAI can meet its obligations through December 31, 2026 with less than USD 250 billion of additional financing beyond the March round. Merely raising less, without establishing ability to pay, is insufficient.
